in_text_mentions: e patient excreted two loose stools. Cardiovascular measurements revealed mild hypotension (BP=105/58 mm Hg) and sinus rhythm on the very edge of tachycardia (HR=96 bpm). Considering the set of hypocortisolism symptoms, immediate treatment with i.v. hydrocortisone was started. The next day, the patient reported a substantial improvement in pain management and a better state of being. Furthermore, serum sodium concentration exceeded 135 mmol/l and neurological ailments resolved. Contrast CT imaging unveiled atrophic morphology of the adrenal glands (figure 1), which led to the diagnosis of aAD.

in_text_mentions: We report a case of a 38‐year‐old man presenting with symptoms of fever for 5 days, associated with generalized weakness, fatigue, and anorexia. Further history revealed that he has had an increased craving for salt. On general examination, pallor, mild icterus, and pigmentation of palms, knuckles, and oral mucosa were noted. Figures 1, 2, 3. None of his family members had similar conditions.

panels.rationale: Single-panel clinical photograph of a human patient's hands and forearms showing diffuse bronze-brown hyperpigmentation with an IV cannula in situ. The article title and in-text confirm Schmidt syndrome (autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2) with pre-existing Addison's disease, and the caption specifically attributes the hand hyperpigmentation to this condition. This is a classic Addisonian manifestation, clearly qualifying for inclusion.
panels.attribution_text: Shahzad and Zaman. Diabetic Ketoacidosis With Schmidt Syndrome: An Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome Type 2.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.81588. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
in_text_mentions: We present a case of a 28-year-old male, already diagnosed with Addison’s disease for the past eight years. He presented to our medical department with nausea and vomiting over two days. On presentation, hyperpigmentation of the gums and skin of the feet and hands was immediately noted when examined (Figures 1-3). His abdomen was soft but mildly tender. Lung fields were clear bilaterally, and no added heart sounds were perceived. Although conscious and oriented, he was lethargic and dehydrated with sunken eyes. He was thus admitted to the medical unit.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of the dorsal hands of a patient diagnosed with Addison's disease in the context of APS-2; the diffuse bronze-brown hyperpigmentation is a classic manifestation of autoimmune adrenal insufficiency. The article title and in-text diagnosis confirm the polyglandular syndrome context, and the caption directly describes the hyperpigmentation shown. B: Clinical photograph of the dorsal feet of the same patient with APS-2 and Addison's disease; the visible hyperpigmentation is a classic Addisonian finding. The caption and in-text diagnosis confirm the disease attribution.

Detailed test results are shown in the accompanying Table 1. Blood glucose levels and electrocardiogram findings were unremarkable, and parathyroid hormone levels were within the normal range.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real human-patient clinical photograph of the abdomen in a case report of Schmidt's Syndrome (APS-2). The caption and in-text explicitly describe hyperpigmentation on the abdomen, consistent with the Addisonian/diffuse skin hyperpigmentation manifestation of APS-2. Abdominal distention and striations are also noted but are not in the vocabulary. B: Real human-patient clinical photograph of the forehead in a case report of Schmidt's Syndrome (APS-2). The caption describes a patch of hyperpigmentation on the forehead, consistent with the Addisonian/diffuse skin hyperpigmentation manifestation of APS-2.
panels.attribution_text: Ismaeel et al. End-Stage Renal Disease in a Patient With Schmidt's Syndrome: A Case Report.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.27342. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: A) Image showing abdominal distention, striations (arrow), and hyperpigmentation; B) Patch of hyperpigmentation visible on the patient's forehead
in_text_mentions: Examination demonstrated an alert and oriented middle-aged individual. All vital signs were within the normal range. On inspection of the abdomen, visible distention, striations, and hyperpigmentation were observed (Figure 1). Palpation demonstrated a soft, non-tender abdomen. A non-resonant note was appreciated on percussion. Normal bowel sounds were heard on auscultation.
